findings.description: The setsid leg of CMP-204 never asserts that the victim was actually frozen. It polls up to 3 s for a `T*` state, then polls up to 4 s for it to clear, then asserts `!= T*`. If `_adv_kill_tree` fails at once inside the `setsid bash -c` body (the body carries only four functions via `declare -f`; any other helper `_adv_kill_tree` or `_adv_tree_pids` calls, such as a logger or a pid-liveness check, is `command not found` there), the victim is never stopped, both loops fall through immediately and the final check passes. CMP-193 guards the same scenario with an explicit "the stub never ran inside the freeze" assertion; this leg has no equivalent, so the property it claims to pin (the CONT watchdog survives a process-group KILL of the reviewer) is not actually exercised on a host where the inlined body cannot run.
findings.failure_mode: A regression that drops the watchdog's own-session detachment, or a refactor that adds a helper to the kill-tree path, leaves this leg green while the guarantee it names is gone; a frozen `claude -p` can then hold the per-binary lock indefinitely after a group kill, exactly the failure the test exists to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Record whether `T*` was observed (set a flag in the first loop) and fail with a message when it was not, mirroring CMP-193; or run the body through `bash -c "$(declare -f $(compgen -A function _adv_))..."` so every script helper is present, and additionally assert the watchdog pid appeared (e.g. via the `wd-calls`-style seam used in CMP-209).

findings.description: CMP-210 ages the `companion.phase` file with `touch -d "@$(( now - 700 ))"` (three times). `-d @<epoch>` is GNU coreutils syntax; BSD/macOS `touch -d` takes an ISO-8601 string and rejects `@…`. The implementation report records that the tenth run removed every GNU-only primitive (`date +%s%N`, `touch -d`, unguarded `flock`) from this suite as a standing rule, and CMP-183 in this same slice is titled as pinning the suite's own portability floor. This test reintroduces the retired primitive with no `skip` guard.
findings.failure_mode: On a non-GNU host the three `touch` calls exit non-zero under bats errexit and CMP-210 reports red for a reason unrelated to the queue-phase bound it tests, breaking the suite's documented contract that GNU-only tooling is either avoided or skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the python3 the suite already requires (`python3 -c 'import os,sys; t=int(sys.argv[2]); os.utime(sys.argv[1],(t,t))' "$T/dq210/companion.phase" $((now-700))`), or drive `_companion_deadline_why` through its fake-clock seam the repair-loop tests use, so no mtime manipulation is needed.
